obligations.note: Ticket CHG-24452 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-14, before review. Its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover all four touched files.
sofia.santos approved the code_review on head 588c867e. She holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author, aisha.bello.
The change has a single commit, and both approvals name that head commit.

run.json claims ci-runner-01 ran on head, starting at the exact commit time. The only JUnit report is from host 'dev-laptop-7.local' with timestamp 2026-10-23T20:29Z, which is after the review time of 2026-10-22T16:09Z. That report cannot be this CI run's output, so there is no valid evidence of the suite or the control tests passing on the final commit.
The change touches security-sensitive payments.http, payments.routes and payments.store. kofi.mensah, a security_reviewer, approved the security_review on head.

Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1) covers routes.py, which this change alters in behaviour, so that evidence has lapsed. The only new evidence offered is the invalid JUnit report, so no replacement evidence of the same exhaustive strength exists.

By inspection, the new POST /payees/{id}/reopen route maps to the privileged action manage_payees with mfa=True and has a handler. However, the exhaustive control test result rests on an untrustworthy report, and the prior ledger evidence has lapsed.

The new reopen_payee operation records an audit event with actor, action, target and time. However, the only test evidence (the sampled control test) comes from the invalid CI report, and no test exercises reopen.
store.py changed, but the new statement touches only status and closed_at, not NPI columns. The exhaustive encryption control test result is not credible evidence because the report is invalid.
The new inline SQL is a fixed string with the id bound as a parameter, which looks compliant. However, the exhaustive SQL control test result depends on the invalid CI report.

summary: Ticket, independent code review, security review and approval coverage are all in order for this single-commit change. The CI evidence is not: the JUnit report is timestamped after the review time and comes from a developer workstation, not the CI executor named in run.json. So there is no valid proof that the suite and control tests passed on the head commit. The MFA-1 ledger evidence lapsed because routes.py changed, and it has not been replaced. The change is rejected under CHG-4 and LAP-1, and the touched product obligations remain unestablished.
